reason: A: both decorative circles were pulled fully inside the canvas, so they look like floating blobs instead of the original's edge-bleeding shapes. The can's right edge sits awkwardly against the teal circle, there is a large dead gap between the CTA and the legal line, and the legal line runs over the bottom circle. B keeps the edge bleeds and a more balanced vertical composition. However, the GLACIER logo now sits on the teal circle, the CTA is jammed tight under the headline, and the legal line floats well above the bottom edge over the circle, leaving an empty strip below it.

A has a sensible left-to-right banner flow (logo, bottle, headline/copy, CTA) with room to breathe. However, the SOLSTICE logo is tiny, the bottle cap jams against the top edge, the body copy is very small and wraps to an orphaned 'sweet.', and the CTA sits awkwardly half over the green circle. B is more readable, but it is badly cramped: both circles are piled into the top-right corner and crowd 'fizz', the oversized CTA nearly touches the right and bottom edges, and the bottle runs almost edge to edge vertically, leaving no breathing room.

A: the headline is shrunk to two long lines that run almost to the side edges, there is a big dead gap between the headline and the CTA so the button looks detached, and the bottom third is empty, so the layout reads as unplanned. B: the headline is set large over four well-balanced lines and the CTA sits close beneath it as one group, which keeps the original's hierarchy; the minor flaw is that the group sits low, with a large top margin and a tight margin below the button.

A: the yellow circle floats as a standalone blob instead of bleeding off the edge as in the original, which leaves the top half dead. The text is crammed into the bottom left, the headline wraps to leave 'here' orphaned on its own line, and the pills and CTA sit as a separate right-hand fragment over the pink circle, so the layout splits in two with a weak headline. B: the headline dominates, the edge-bleeding circles keep the original's feel and the pills form one clean row. But the headline's left edge doesn't line up with the logo and subhead, the headline nearly touches the right edge, and the CTA floats between the subhead and the pills on an arbitrary right alignment.

A keeps the circle, can, headline, subhead and buttons grouped as in the original with clear hierarchy. But the whole block sits in the top ~60%, leaving a large empty orange band at the bottom. The NEW badge and Try It button are also cramped right under the subhead, and the CTA is undersized. B breaks the product art: the cream circle has come apart from the can and sits clipped in the bottom-left corner. The orange can blends into the orange background, the NEW badge is stranded in the top-right corner, and the headline is small. The headline, subhead and CTA float with arbitrary gaps and no shared alignment.

A: the legal line floats in the middle of the canvas, sitting on the bottom-left circle, and leaves about 100px of dead space below it. The teal circle is fully contained rather than bleeding off the corner, and it sits behind the logo and can, which loses the original's framing. B: the legal line is correctly anchored at the bottom, but the content is top-heavy, with a roughly 220px empty gap between the CTA and the legal line. The shrunken teal circle just touches the can's right edge, an awkward near-collision, and both circles are contained rather than bleeding off the edges. Both keep the hierarchy and brand, and B's layout reads a little more conventionally.

A reads well left to right (logo, bottle, headline/body, CTA) and its text is readable. However, it is cramped: the bottle nearly touches the top and bottom edges, the oversized CTA crowds the right and bottom edges and competes with the headline, and the stacked circles butt against 'fizz'. B has a tiny, weak SOLSTICE logo and body copy too small to read at this size, with an orphaned 'sweet.' line. Its bottle is jammed against the top and bottom edges, and a big empty middle leaves the elements scattered, so it is the worse of the two.

A rewraps the headline into four bold lines that fill the portrait width and keeps the CTA close beneath it, so the hierarchy and feel of the original survive. Its only flaw is that the group sits a little low: there is about 50px below the CTA against about 170px of space at the top. B leaves the headline small and nearly edge to edge (side margins of about 35px), opens a gap of about 190px that cuts the CTA off from its copy, and leaves a dead band at the bottom, so the portrait canvas looks unused rather than redesigned.

A has a strong hierarchy with a big headline and a clear CTA, but its left edges don't line up: the logo and subhead sit at x≈76 while the headline sits at x≈64. The headline almost touches the right edge, the CTA floats above the flavour chips so the reading order is off, and the pink circle is cropped awkwardly at the top right. B breaks the headline badly, leaving 'here' alone on its own line. Its top half is mostly empty apart from a yellow blob that has nothing to do with the rest, the text is crammed into the bottom left, and the chips form an uneven two-plus-one grid on top of the pink circle, so the right-hand cluster feels arbitrary and the layout is badly balanced.

A pulls the art apart: the cream circle is cut off in the bottom-left corner, so the can sits bare on orange and its outline almost disappears. The headline is small for the canvas, the NEW badge floats alone in the top-right, and the headline, subline and button are spaced loosely with no shared edges, so the layout looks scattered. B keeps the circle, the can and the brand look together, with a strong headline, then subline, then badge and button. However, it leaves the bottom third of the canvas empty, so the content looks top-heavy. The NEW pill is close in weight to the Try It button, and the text in the button sits slightly low.

A keeps the original's order (CITRINE, large bag, headline, CTA) on a clear centre axis, with good scale and the decorative circles in the corners. Its flaws are that 'fizz' drops onto its own line as an orphan, and the CTA sits fairly close under the headline while there is extra empty space at the bottom. B shrinks the bag and squeezes CITRINE inside the green circle, then leaves a large dead gap between the headline and a CTA that has become tiny and overlaps the olive circle. That separates the CTA from its copy, buries it, and makes the layout look unbalanced and unplanned.

A squashes the round backdrop into a tall oval that runs nearly edge to edge, which distorts the key image. Its can label is unreadably small, and the badges and CTA sit at the top of the right column with dead space under them, so the layout looks top-heavy. B keeps the circle and can in proportion and gives the headline strong two-line prominence. Its flaws: the GLACIER wordmark floats centred and doesn't align with the headline's left edge, and the badge/CTA cluster is pushed down against the bottom edge, out of line with the text column. Both still need fixes before shipping.

A keeps the original structure: a large two-line centred headline with the LIMITED tag and CTA pill grouped below it, so the hierarchy and brand stay intact. Its flaws are small: the headline sits a little close to the top edge, the line break leaves 'botanicals' alone on the first line, and the badge-plus-button group is slightly off the headline's centre axis, as in the original. B shrinks the headline to one thin centred line but moves the badge and CTA to the left edge, which mixes two alignment systems. The CTA is jammed against the bottom edge and the oversized LIMITED badge competes with the button, leaving a large empty area on the right.

A: the product bag is shrunk and pushed into the top third, with CITRINE squeezed inside the green circle. There is a huge dead gap between the headline and the CTA. The 'Find a Store' button is small, which buries the call to action, and it collides with the olive circle. B: keeps the original's top-to-bottom stack with a well-sized product, headline and CTA, and the circles stay as corner accents. Its main flaw is the headline wrap, which leaves 'fizz' orphaned on its own line. The CTA also sits a little tight under the headline.

A keeps the circle round and has a strong two-line headline, but the GLACIER wordmark floats off-axis instead of lining up with the headline. The circle presses against the top edge, the CTA nearly touches the bottom edge and the two badge pills almost touch each other. B lines up the wordmark, headline and body copy well, but the circle is stretched into an ellipse that gets cut off at the top and bottom. The SOLSTICE label on the can is illegible, and all the content sits in the upper half, leaving a dead band of empty space underneath.

A: the headline is shrunk to one centred line, but the LIMITED badge and CTA are stacked flush-left underneath it, so the layout has two axes that clash. The badge is oversized and nearly as heavy as the CTA, and the right side is left empty. B: it keeps the original's centred structure with a large two-line headline and the badge+CTA pairing intact, but the whole group sits too high (the headline almost touches the top edge) and leaves dead space at the bottom. The tiny LIMITED badge text is barely readable.

A has no consistent alignment: the GROVE wordmark is centred, the headline and body copy are left-aligned, and the badges and CTA are pushed to the right. The badges nearly touch, and the text block drifts off any shared edge. B sits on a clean left grid with a full-width CTA, but it has its own flaws. GROVE is blown up until it competes with the headline, and 'back' is left alone on the headline's last line. The FREE DELIVERY badge has been dropped below the CTA, crammed near the bottom edge, which makes it look like an afterthought. The shoe also sits high inside its circle, leaving the bottom of the circle empty.

A: The four-line headline fills the square with strong presence. The bottom row is the problem: the body copy is centre-aligned in a cramped left column and its left edge (~97px) doesn't line up with the headline (~125px), while the CTA sits off to the right. That breaks the original's single centred axis and leaves the bottom crowded under a heavy headline. B: A faithful centred stack with clear hierarchy, readable text and nothing colliding. But it is basically the original lifted onto the square, with large empty orange bands above (~225px) and below (~200px), a single-line subline that runs almost edge to edge, and a slightly jagged edge on the CTA pill. B is cleaner and more coherent overall.

A is the better resize. It rebuilds the layout for the tall format: the headline is large, the bottle is the centrepiece and the CTA is prominent. It still has flaws. 'WEEKEND ONLY' has moved from above the headline to below the body copy, which breaks the original reading order. The body copy wraps so that 'sparkling.' sits alone on its own line. The headline sits partly over the circle, and the top margin is uneven. B simply keeps the original's top cluster at small size, with a small bottle tucked into the circle. That leaves a huge empty dead zone in the middle of the canvas and the CTA stranded alone near the bottom. The layout looks unfinished and suits the tall format poorly.

I picked A, but only narrowly. Its large CTA keeps the hierarchy, but the phone is clipped at the top and bottom. The badge and CTA row sits almost on the bottom edge and leaves the area to the right of the headline empty. B is more balanced as a banner, but its phone is cropped hard top and bottom. Its 'Try It' CTA has shrunk to the same size as the 'Online Only' badge, so the action no longer stands out. The badge and CTA are also stacked tightly against the right edge.

A is broken: the orange can graphic sits right on top of the TASTINGS/ALL AGES pills, the RSVP button and the URL line, so the main call to action is tangled up with an illustration. The decorative sun circle has also been blown up behind the whole text block, and the bottom third is empty apart from the missing-asset placeholder. B keeps the original's structure with no collisions and a clear headline → details → RSVP order, but it is a near-uniform shrink rather than a real rearrangement: the logo, pills and URL text are small, the can is pushed to the right edge, and the bottom quarter is dead space with the visible missing-asset placeholder.

A keeps one clean left edge for the whole text stack, but the headline breaks badly and leaves 'back' alone on its own line. The GROVE wordmark has been made much bigger and bolder, losing the original's small tracked style. The FREE DELIVERY tag is stuck below the CTA near the bottom edge, and the pills sit too close to the CTA. B wraps the headline well and keeps the tag top-right, but mixes three alignments with no logic: GROVE is centred, the headline and body copy are left-aligned, and the pills and CTA are pushed right. The CTA floats off the text column and the layout looks unplanned.

A keeps the original's centred stack (headline, subline, CTA) with clear hierarchy and even spacing. Its flaws: the headline is undersized for a square canvas, the margins above and below are large and empty, and the button edges look slightly jagged. B makes a strong 4-line headline but crams the subline and CTA side by side at the bottom. That subline wraps raggedly onto 3 centred lines with an awkward break ('Now in / four flavours'). Neither the subline nor the CTA lines up with the headline's centre axis, and the bottom row sits tight against the bottom edge, which breaks the reading flow.

A is just the original shrunk into the top third. Copy and bottle are crammed together, the CTA is stranded at the bottom, and about 250px of dead space sits between them. The headline and body copy are small for a story format. B is a proper vertical rearrangement with a strong headline, a large bottle and a prominent CTA. But the 'WEEKEND ONLY' eyebrow is moved below the body copy, which breaks the reading order. The left-aligned text clashes with the centred bottle and button, and 'sparkling.' wraps onto its own line.

A has clean margins and centred copy, but the stacked right column makes the 'ONLINE ONLY' badge the same size and weight as the shrunken 'Try It' button, so the CTA is buried and competes with a secondary badge. The large phone also crowds the left side. B gives the CTA clear priority and a natural headline → subline → action order, but it is cramped: the headline sits about 20px from the top, the CTA nearly touches the bottom edge, and the phone is jammed against the copy with dead space under it.

A is mostly the original shrunk down rather than rearranged. Its text is smaller, and the FREE ENTRY / ALL AGES / TASTINGS chips are barely readable at this size. The bottom third is empty apart from the stray partner-placeholder box, and the decorative circle is cut off at the top-left. Still, there are no collisions and the hierarchy matches the original. B is clearly broken: the product can is placed on top of the ALL AGES chip, the RSVP Free button and the 'Reserve a spot' line, so the call to action and its supporting copy collide with the image. The big centred circle is a nice idea, but the bottom of the canvas is left empty.

A breaks the hero apart: the green circle sits alone, cropped, at the far left, and the can floats tiny at the far right, leaving dead space between them. The SOLSTICE wordmark has dropped below the headline, the CTA is shrunk to a small pill in a row with the badges so it no longer stands out, and the body copy is too small to read. B keeps the can on its circle at the left, puts the brand above the headline and gives the CTA real weight at the right end, so it reads left to right as a banner should. Its flaws: the circle is cropped into a squashed oval, the body copy is still tiny and wraps 'battles.' onto its own line, and the badges float in the middle, cut off from the copy.

A reads cleanly from left to right: brand, then the one-line headline, then the badges, then the CTA. But the phone and its circle are cut off at the top and bottom edges, the 'Find It Near You' button is jammed against the right edge with its text almost touching the button's sides, and the tagline is tiny. B keeps the phone whole but leaves it isolated, with a big dead gap before the copy. 'SOLSTICE' floats off to the left of the headline instead of sitting above it, the two-line headline is cramped, and the badges and CTA are stacked in an odd 2x2 grid that makes the CTA the same width as a badge, so it no longer stands out as the action.

A: the product can is shrunk to a tiny scrap, and the Shop Sale button covers most of it and its circle, so the hero image is lost. Everything is crammed into the top third, leaving about 55% of the canvas empty above the tiny legal line. B rearranges the design properly for the tall shape: headline, then CTA, then a large product, then the legal line, in the original colours. Its flaws: '20% off' runs almost to the right edge, the purple circle sits awkwardly behind the headline instead of framing the product, the legal text is too big compared with the subhead, and the left margin is uneven.

A is broken. The white headline sits on the cream circle and is barely readable, 'Orange Sunset' runs into the bottle, and the 'Try It' button covers the bottle label and cuts off the 'C' of COLD. B has no collisions and its text is readable, but it has clear flaws. The bottle is a tiny thumbnail jammed into the top-left corner and spills past its circle at the top edge. The NEW badge is nearly as heavy as the CTA. The right-aligned badge and CTA don't line up with the left-aligned headline, which leaves a dead area in the bottom-left.

I'd ship neither, but B is less bad. In A, the 'Reserve a spot' caption runs into the bottom edge of the RSVP button, and the subtitle is indented away from the headline's edge. The details, pills and CTA are crammed together under the headline, the placeholder box sits on top of the decorative circle, and the logo is tiny and stuck out on its own. B uses a sensible three-column banner with a strong headline, but its middle column is ragged: the date, time, pills and caption all start at slightly different points. 'Sessions' nearly touches the middle column, the legal text is tiny and jammed against the bottom edge, and the placeholder box is crowded against the phone.

A: the headline sits right on top of the shrunken shoe and circle, so the text collides with a busy image. The NEW VIDEO badge overlaps the circle, everything is crammed into the top quarter, and about 60% of the canvas below is empty purple. B is a proper vertical restack (brand and badge, then headline, then hero shoe, then subline) with nothing colliding and the brand intact. Its flaws are minor: 'Full review inside.' is jammed between the circle and the bottom edge, and the circle and shoe fill the lower area a bit tightly.

A reads left to right as a banner should: can, brand, headline, badges, then a prominent CTA on the right. Its flaws are that the body copy is so small it's barely readable, the backdrop circle is clipped at the top and bottom edges, and the badges float in the middle, cut off from their copy. B splits the product art apart, leaving an empty green circle on the left and a bare can stranded on the far right. It also puts the headline above the SOLSTICE wordmark, shrinks the CTA into a small pill in the badge row so it's buried, and its body text is tiny and illegible.

A: the SOLSTICE wordmark floats to the left of the two-line headline instead of sitting above it. The badges are blown up to the same size as the CTA, and the CTA is stacked under a badge, so hierarchy is muddled. There is a dead gap between the phone and the text, and empty space trails off to the right. B: it reads left to right like a proper banner, with a one-line headline and the badges in a row leading to the CTA. However, the background circle is stretched into an oval, the phone touches the top and bottom edges, and the CTA is jammed against the right edge with its label nearly filling the pill.

A is a coherent vertical stack: headline, CTA, then product. Its flaws are that '20% off' is oversized and runs almost to the right edge, the cropped circle sits behind 'WEEKEND ONLY' and the headline, and the footer is nearly as large as the subhead. B shrinks the product to a tiny scrap, and the full-width CTA covers its lower half. The copy is jammed into the top third above a huge empty middle, and the fine print is lost at the bottom, so B is unusable.

A: text is readable and nothing collides, but the bottle sticks out of the top of its circle and almost touches the canvas edge. The headline is left-aligned while the NEW pill and the oversized Try It button are pushed to the right, which leaves a large empty area at the bottom left, so the layout has no clear grid. B: the white headline sits on the cream circle and runs into the dark bottle, so it is nearly unreadable. The Try It button also overlaps the bottle, which makes this layout unusable.

A has a clear left-to-right banner structure: logo, a large headline in the left column, then date, chips and CTA in the middle, with the phone on the right. Its flaws are small and need fixing: '6 pm' is indented a few pixels from 'Saturday 21 June', the legal text is tiny and crammed under the CTA, and the placeholder box floats next to the phone. B has real collisions: the 'Reserve a spot' line sits on the bottom edge of the RSVP button, and the placeholder box overlaps the phone. B also indents the subtitle for no reason, packs the date, chips and CTA tightly under the headline, and crams the logo into the corner, so its hierarchy is weaker and the layout looks jammed.

A rebuilds the layout properly for the tall format: the logo and NEW VIDEO badge sit in a top row, then the large headline wraps cleanly over three lines, then the lime circle with the shoe, then the 'Full review inside.' line. Small flaws: the badge is a little tilted and crowds the top-right corner, the circle is slightly off-centre, and the space below the circle is tight. In B, the headline sits directly on top of the shrunken shoe/circle graphic and the badge overlaps the circle, both clear collisions. The hero image is squeezed into the top-right corner, and roughly two-thirds of the canvas is empty purple above a lone 'Full review inside.' line, so B can't be used.
